title: maestro-state-manager 'answers received' transition calls writeState(state) without sessionId — the interviewComplete flag is written to the default (non-session) state file, so the session-scoped read on the next prompt never sees it
telemetry: Maestro stuck at interview phase after the user answers AskUserQuestion: next prompt's readState(sessionId) returns interviewComplete=false because the flag landed in the default-session file.
observe_how: Compare the two writeState call sites: every other call passes sessionId; line 348 omits it, so getStateFile(undefined) resolves to a different path than getStateFile(sessionId).

title: Two divergent output contracts across the 12 UserPromptSubmit hooks: half emit ad-hoc {result:'continue',message}/{result:'block',reason}, half emit the documented hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext — the repo's own docs call additionalContext 'the reliable inject pattern', so the {result,message} hooks' context (maestro suggestion, skill activation, ralph progress, guardrail 'block') may never reach Claude
telemetry: If {result,message} is ignored by the current Claude Code version, maestro-detector suggestions, skill-activation banners, ralph progress bars, and guardrail 'blocks' silently never appear in model context despite the hooks running.
observe_how: Emit a known sentinel string from a {result,message} hook and grep the session transcript/additionalContext for it; compare against a hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext emit. Confirms which shape Claude Code honors for UserPromptSubmit.

title: smarter-everyday reads Bash output as tool_response.output ONLY — if the harness delivers stdout/stderr, test success/failure is never detected, the state machine dead-ends in TESTING, and the entire 'victory library' silently captures nothing
causal_links: if dead, contributes to low WORKING_SOLUTION density behind memory-recall hit-rate 27.4%

evidence.quote: const output = String((toolResponse as { output?: string })?.output || '');

observe_how: Sibling hook git-commit-roadmap defends against BOTH Bash payload shapes (.output then .stdout); smarter-everyday and roadmap-completion's handleBashOutput read .output only. If the runtime delivers {stdout,stderr}, output is '' so isTestSuccess/isTestFailure both return false; the machine transitions ATTEMPTING→TESTING and TESTING has no outbound transitions anywhere in processTransition (CANDIDATE is only reachable from ATTEMPTING with detected success), so no victory is ever stored. Cheap observation: query archival_memory for tags LIKE '%victory%' — zero rows since deployment confirms the dead-end; any rows disconfirm. Also doc drift: header says state lives at .claude/smarter-everyday-state.json but getStateFilePath returns getSessionStatePath('smarter-everyday') (temp dir). Fix: read output || stdout (+stderr) like git-commit-roadmap, and add a TESTING fallback transition.
telemetry: Registered on Edit|Write|Bash|TaskUpdate (4-tool matcher = high fire rate) — full state-file read/write cycle per event even while the victory path may be unreachable

title: prd-roadmap-sync path containment uses startsWith prefix comparison — sibling dirs sharing the prefix (continuous-claude-x) bypass the guard; one-line path.relative fix
causal_links: D2d-09 (same hook's write path makes the weak guard matter)
observe_how: Payoff: replacing with a path.relative(projectDir, filePath) '..'-check closes both the sibling-prefix bypass (C:\...\continuous-claude-evil passes for projectDir C:\...\continuous-claude) and Windows drive-letter case mismatch false rejections — the same bug class the Codex adversary caught in the Phase A bus code.

title: import-validator: module-path verification compares forward-slash expectedModule against TLDR daemon result paths — on Windows (backslash daemon paths) the includes() check can never match, turning every resolvable local import into a false 'imported from X but defined in Y' warning

evidence.quote: warnings.push(`${symbol}: imported from ${imp.module} but defined in ${actualFile}`);

observe_how: INFERRED because the TLDR daemon's result.file separator format was not traced. If daemon paths use '\\' (native Windows), 'scripts/core/recall' never substring-matches 'scripts\\core\\recall_learnings.py' and the hook injects a wrong-location warning for a CORRECT import — a false claim in context (would be S1 if confirmed). Verify with one daemon search on Windows; fix is normalizing check.location separators before includes(). Also note the substring heuristic ('def <symbol>' FTS) false-positives on same-named local symbols shadowing stdlib imports.
telemetry: rate of '[Import check]' injections on imports that actually resolve (pyright clean)

title: web-lookup-advisor: failure heuristic misfires — `response == null` treated as failure (payload-shape dependent) and the word-match regex flags short SUCCESSFUL responses containing 'error'/'failed'/'not found'

evidence.quote:
// Null/undefined response is a failure
  if (response == null) return true;

observe_how: Payoff: a search result like 'No errors found in 3 sources' (<500 chars) injects a spurious opencli redirect — context noise of the same family the 24.6% intent-pollution telemetry tracks.
telemetry: rate of opencli suggestions following 2xx WebFetch/WebSearch

title: session-start-docker: isDockerAvailable() runs execSync('docker info') with NO timeout — a wedged Docker Desktop engine pins the hook until its 30s registration timeout on every session open
observe_how: Every other execSync in this file passes a timeout (e.g. line 83 timeout: 10000, line 113 timeout: 3000); only the availability probe omits it. With Docker Desktop in its half-started state, `docker info` blocks for tens of seconds and the hook holds the session-open gate to the full 30s. Happy path still costs two docker CLI calls (~0.5-1.5s).
telemetry: Reproducible by pausing Docker Desktop engine and starting a session: session open stalls ~30s before SQLite-fallback message.
